the development of a new, simple method for the direct determination and speciation of inorganic cations, such as Na+, Mg2+, and K+, in proteinaceous samples, without any sample pretreatment.
the determination of small inorganics in samples containing large amount of proteins, such a milk, using capillary electrophoreses.
the direct determination of inorganic cations (Na(+), K(+), Ca(2+), Mg(2+)) in samples containing large concentrations of proteins.

the direct determination of inorganic cations by CE is possible, provided that the electrolyte composition is carefully selected.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a flow injection analysis-CE system with a selected electrolyte allows the direct determination of inorganic cations (K+, Na+) in samples containing large protein concentrations, without the use of sample pretreatment.

the use of an electrokinetic injection step, in combination with the selected capillary electrolyte, enables the direct determination of trace amounts of small cations (i.e. Na+ and K+) in proteinaceous samples.
a simple dilution step is sufficient for determining the cation content of proteinaceous samples, which is of great importance in food and biomedical applications.
